title: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Salary: A Guide for NSW Teacher Salary
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual salary using the 38-hour week. Includes tax, super, and the NSW teacher salary context.
salarySummary: Annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by hours per week (usually 38) times 52 weeks.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52. For a standard full-time role of 38 hours, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. If you work different hours, adjust the weekly figure accordingly.

faqs.q: What tax and Medicare levy apply to a NSW teacher salary?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, resident tax rates are: nil up to $18,200, 15% from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000, and 45% above that. Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. Use these brackets on your annual gross pay after any deductions. The exact tax depends on your total income and circumstances.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on an annual salary?
faqs.a: Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary. For example, if your annual gross is $80,000, your employer contributes an extra $9,600 into super, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional benefit.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Salary

If you know your hourly rate, you can estimate your annual gross pay using a simple formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. This article explains how to do that, what it means for your take-home pay, and how it relates to the **NSW teacher salary** context.

### The Basic Formula

Most full-time roles in Australia are based on a 38-hour week. So the standard calculation is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, if you earn $30 per hour, your annual gross would be $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. This assumes you work the same hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It is a starting point for budgeting and comparing job offers.

If you work a different number of hours each week, use your average weekly hours. Part-time or casual workers can still use this formula with their usual weekly hours.

### The Fortnightly View

Many Australians are paid fortnightly. To get your fortnightly gross, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the example above, weekly pay is $30 × 38 = $1,140, so fortnightly gross is $2,280. This can help you match your budget to your pay cycle.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The **National Minimum Wage** from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Some awards and enterprise agreements set higher rates. For example, the **NSW teacher salary** is governed by the Crown Employees (Teachers in Schools and Related Employees) Award. While we do not have a specific median figure here, the average full-time weekly earnings in New South Wales (May 2026) are $2,108.80 – this is an average across all occupations, not the median for a NSW teacher salary. Always check your award or agreement for your exact rate.

### Casual Loading

If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. The casual minimum wage from 1 July 2026 is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). When using our [timesheet](/), you can check a box to add 25% casual loading. Do not enter a rate that already includes the loading – enter the base rate and let the calculator add it.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Once you have your annual gross, you can estimate tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- 15% on income from $18,201 – $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 – $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 – $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. For example, on a gross of $80,000, tax (before offsets) would be approximately $5,092 + $10,500 = $15,592, plus Medicare of $1,600. Your actual tax may differ due to deductions, offsets, or the Medicare levy surcharge. See our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for more detail.

### Superannuation

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. It does not reduce your take-home pay. For a gross annual salary of $80,000, your employer contributes an extra $9,600 into super, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not included in your annual gross pay – it is additional. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Putting It Together for a NSW Teacher Salary

If you are a NSW teacher, your hourly rate may be set by the award. To convert that to annual salary, use the formula above. Remember that the average full-time weekly earnings in NSW ($2,108.80) is not the median for teachers – it is an average across all industries. For a more accurate picture, refer to your specific award or enterprise agreement. You can also use our [reference tables](/data) to compare rates.

### Important Notes

- This estimate assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice.
- Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base.
- Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here.
- HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted.

This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax. For personalised advice, consult a tax professional or the Australian Taxation Office.
